name: Kalaburagi
headline: Out-of-school counts differ 50-fold between departments, and child marriage is widespread.
summary: A rural-development survey found 11,137 out-of-school children in Kalaburagi while the education department reported 225, so the true scale is unclear. Authorities stopped 128 child marriages in a year and logged 43 more cases in four months, and parents were booked for marrying 15-year-old daughters. Child labour in ragpicking and scrap shops is reported, and the district ranked last in SSLC 2026.

reasons.detail: Officials prevented 128 child marriages in one year and logged 43 more cases in four months; parents were booked for marrying ailing 15-year-olds.
A rural-development survey counted 11,137 out-of-school children against 225 reported by the education department, hiding the real scale.

Officials explaining the 2019 absenteeism survey named migration and ill health as main causes; a Kalaburagi social worker says poor families move to Bengaluru or Mumbai for jobs, interrupting schooling.

A Kalaburagi school teacher describes two-teacher schools with combined classes and unpenalised teacher absence; an RTE activist says teacher vacancies are highest in Kalyana Karnataka districts including Kalaburagi.
District finished last in the 2025 SSLC at 42.43%; sources link weak results to poverty, stunting and anaemia among children, though no study ties these to dropout directly.
A Kalaburagi slum teacher says families marry girls at 16 or 17 rather than keep them in school, fearing elopement; an activist says child marriage has risen. Anecdotal, not survey-based.
A Kalaburagi teacher says scarce water leaves school toilets unusable, so girls go home at lunch and do not return. Reported as a single teacher's account.
Teachers and activists report parents keeping children out to work in fields, and boys skipping school to join local political rallies, so absences stretch beyond a week.

responses.text: A campaign and task force stepped up child-marriage prevention, with officials told to file FIRs swiftly.
In May 2025 the Chief Minister ordered notices to district education deputy directors in districts under 60% SSLC pass rate, which included Kalaburagi.
State-wide 2025 SSLC guidelines (applicable to Kalaburagi) require daily attendance tracking and teacher home visits to students absent over seven days.
